prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: struggling to pay the mortgage. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the monthly payment is close to the household’s spare income, I slow down and test the case against a realistic rise in rates or bills, temporary or ongoing, because a short-term shock is handled very differently from a structural shortfall."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a case includes existing arrears, I prefer to see a clear plan for clearing them before completion or remortgage, because arrears often signal that the payment is already unsustainable."},{"type":"observation","content":"When someone’s income has recently changed, I compare the new income against their committed spending rather than relying on the old budget, because a pay cut, reduced hours or a gap between jobs can leave the mortgage affordable only on paper."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the customer is juggling unsecured borrowing as well as the mortgage, I look for whether the debt repayments are the real pressure point, because high card or loan costs can be the reason the mortgage is becoming hard to maintain."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the household budget depends on overtime, bonuses or variable commission, I treat those amounts cautiously, because they may help in good months but not when the mortgage payment falls due."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a case involves a remortgage with payment difficulty, I like to see the purpose clearly explained, because term extensions, rate changes or debt consolidation can either ease the pressure or simply postpone it."},{"type":"observation","content":"When essential costs have risen sharply, I check whether the customer has already cut back on non-essentials, because a budget that is already stripped back
